title: SK Hynix books record Q3 as HBM memory sells out through 2029
subtitle: The Korean memory maker posted KRW 104.6 trillion in revenue and a roughly 80% operating margin, with 14 long-term supply agreements locking in HBM capacity for the AI buildout.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: SK Hynix reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of KRW 104.62 trillion on October 28, the first time its quarterly revenue has crossed the 100-trillion-won line, with operating profit up 38% from the prior quarter and an operating margin near 80%. The company said DRAM and high-bandwidth memory output is effectively sold out through 2029 under 14 long-term supply agreements with major cloud and chip customers. SK Hynix also projected that HBM4 will surpass HBM3E in both shipments and revenue in Q4 2026, with the figures preliminary pending the independent audit.

An 80% operating margin at this revenue scale is extraordinary. It confirms that memory, not just logic silicon, is a bottleneck for AI training and inference — and that SK Hynix is capturing most of the value sitting in that bottleneck. The 2029 forward-sold position matters because it means a near-term AI capex slowdown cannot easily derail the cycle: the orders are placed, deliveries are scheduled, payments are coming. Bernstein estimates Samsung generated about $8.7 billion in HBM revenue in the same quarter, up 33% quarter over quarter but still trailing SK Hynix's share.

HBM — high-bandwidth memory stacked beside or on top of the GPU — has emerged as the single largest cost constraint on frontier training. Nvidia's and AMD's accelerators cannot ship without it, and Amazon's Trainium and Google's TPUs need it just as badly. SK Hynix's record quarter sits alongside TSMC's recent high and Alphabet's doubled Cloud revenue as evidence that the AI capex buildout is still accelerating, even as the chip-exposed Nasdaq saw a roughly 6% pullback from its early-October peak on AI-returns concerns.

A takeaway for learners: when a company at this scale posts an 80% operating margin, the lesson is less about the specific product and more about the shape of the AI value chain. The scarce input earns the outsized margin — and HBM is scarce because stacking memory dies with the thermal and signal integrity needed for AI accelerators is genuinely hard engineering. If you want to work at the heart of the AI buildout, memory packaging and advanced interconnects (CoWoS, HBM4, custom fabric) are where the demand curve is steepest for the next five years.
